blockers.title: The architecture selector is not bound to the payload executed by the PE entry point
evidence: The x86 branch checks four setup_header facts and then accepts any nonzero in-member range computed from payload_offset and payload_length. It does not require that range to be in a loadable PE section, exclude the certificate table or overlay, validate the PE machine/entry point as the corresponding Linux EFI stub, or establish that the entry point consumes and transfers control to that range.

The arm64 zboot branch says only to locate a zimg header and keep its payload range inside the member. It does not restrict the header or payload to a loaded section or bind either to the PE entry point. The uncompressed branch's phrase 'section that contains the arm64 Image text' supplies no byte grammar or control-transfer join.

neverSearchRawWrapper constrains only where IKCFG markers are searched after selection. It does not prevent setup_header or a zimg record from designating inert wrapper, overlay, or certificate bytes as the selected payload; once designated, those bytes are no longer 'outside the selected payload' under the literal rule.

Concrete counterexample: an authenticated, measured PE has an entry point that boots kexec-capable code from its executable sections. Its four x86 setup fields, or a unique arm64 zimg-shaped record, designate an inert in-member range Q containing one valid-looking disabled IKCONFIG blob. The member sha256, Authenticode digest, manifest joins, signed kexecCapability, and signed ikconfigDigest all bind the same PE and Q, so every stated equality passes, while the entry point never executes Q and the running kernel can kexec into undeclared M.

Exact-byte authentication proves which wrapper firmware measured; it does not prove the new selector chose the wrapper's executed kernel payload. The claimed 'loaded/decompressed' property is therefore asserted rather than derived.
blockers.impact: A measured and exactly authenticated PE can qualify from inert safe-looking bytes while executing a kexec-capable kernel. Post-boot replacement can introduce undeclared OS-ABI code, leaving the platform TCB open.
blockers.requiredRepair: Pin a versioned canonical x86 and arm64 image grammar that joins the selected payload to the actual PE machine, loaded section map, entry point/EFI-stub path, and transfer target. Reject payloads in the certificate table, overlay, or other non-loaded ranges, and reject a wrapper whose entry path can bypass the selected payload. Add decoy-header and entrypoint-bypass negative vectors, not only raw IKCFG-decoy vectors.

blockers.title: The IKCONFIG digest authenticates mutable data, not the configuration that compiled the executable code
evidence: The field named complete does not define a kernel release/Kconfig symbol universe, a full serialization, a builder statement, or any relation between C and compilation. Its literal grammar accepts C containing only CONFIG_IKCONFIG=y and the five requiredN symbols in disabled form.

A concrete 168-byte C with exactly those six lines satisfies every stated line, uniqueness, CONFIG_IKCONFIG, and requiredN condition. Gzipping it produces one IKCFG_ST/IKCFG_ED pair and its accepted C digest is b2868a1d4b784e2051d0de261c3a4b861851ba52d8df396d1444661bc6510ccc.

IKCONFIG is an embedded data blob. A kexec-enabled payload can have its one blob replaced or patched after link so C says the five symbols are disabled while the already-emitted kexec-capable machine code is unchanged. The v37 rule does not require signed builder provenance saying that C governed compilation, a reproducible-build relation, or an independent code capability proof.

The exact member hashes and signed ikconfigDigest authenticate the inconsistent binary and the patched C. The inventory signer is required only to echo the derivation result and digest; signing the result does not establish the missing build relation. v37 itself says signed carriage MUST NOT replace derivation, so the signature cannot cure this false derivation.

This is the selected-payload form of PTCB-V36-B1: moving the marker inside P and requiring explicit lines removes the raw-wrapper and omission attacks, but not the inert-data-versus-compiled-code attack or the predecessor's required build-provenance bind.
blockers.impact: A kexec-capable exact kernel payload can be qualified as kexec-absent and later replace itself with an undeclared kernel. The signed digest makes the false claim reproducible but does not close the OS-ABI TCB.
blockers.requiredRepair: Bind the exact C digest to the exact executable member through signed build provenance from the builder and a pinned build/config identity relation, or replace IKCONFIG inspection with an independently verifiable code-capability proof. Define what a complete version-appropriate configuration is; an inventory signature over a mechanically extracted blob is not build provenance. Add a vector whose sole official-looking IKCONFIG blob disagrees with the compiled capability.

shouldFix.title: The arm64 selection and decompression grammar remains contradictory and underdetermined
evidence: The zboot rule says zero zimg headers refuses, while the immediately adjacent uncompressedImage rule says no zimg header selects the uncompressed fallback. The same input is therefore both a mandatory refusal and the trigger for a valid branch.

The zboot text does not state the scan domain for the header or the base relative to which payload_offset is applied. 'payload range MUST lie wholly inside the member' does not resolve whether the offset is member-relative or header-relative.

compressed_type is accepted from the header, while decompress independently detects a compressor by payload magic; no equality or precedence rule resolves a disagreement. The none branch has no detection grammar even though other magics refuse.

The uncompressed selector does not define how a section is proven to contain 'the arm64 Image text'. The generic unique-executable-section parenthetical is not an arm64 Image header parse and can disagree with the section layout of an otherwise valid PE.

The outer decompressor has a 128 MiB output limit, but the nested IKCONFIG gunzip has no output limit and no single-member, concatenated-member, or trailing-byte rule. Independent gzip APIs can produce different C values from the same bytes.
shouldFix.impact: Conforming implementations can disagree on acceptance, selected bytes, compressor, and C; valid arm64 machines can be unqualifiable, and ambiguous selection feeds the blocker in PTCB-V37-B1.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: State a single zero/one/many zimg decision tree; pin the header search domain, offset base, header bounds, compressor-field/magic equality, none selection, arm64 Image header/section selection, and inner-gzip EOF/resource rules. Provide positive and malformed vectors for every branch and disagreement case.

shouldFix.title: The new two-component derivation result is not propagated consistently through the closed records and negative test
evidence: kexecAbsenceDerivation.output is now 'the token kexec-absent plus ikconfigDigest', a two-component result.

authenticatedKernelMember remains the exact shape {relativePath, sha256, peCoffImageDigest, kexecCapability, gnuBuildId?} and still requires its scalar kexecCapability to equal the entire derivation output. signedObject.kexecCapability and laterEventVariant.kexecCapability repeat the same scalar-to-pair equality.

signedObject adds ikconfigDigest, but laterEventVariant and the tag-level join retain and compare only kexecCapability. They do not name a later ikconfigDigest or an explicit direct signedObject-to-derived-digest comparison in that closed join.
NT-TCB-KEXEC refuses signed kexecCapability mismatch but omits signed ikconfigDigest mismatch; the reserved G22 parser-vector list omits that mismatch too, even though refusesBootConfigs names it.

A literal implementation cannot make a scalar token equal a pair. A projection-based implementation can, but the contract does not state the projection consistently, so implementations can silently drop or differently place the digest check.
shouldFix.impact: The closed schema is internally inconsistent and independent implementations can disagree about whether and where the new signed digest must be retained and compared.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define a closed structured derivation result such as {kexecCapability, ikconfigDigest}; compare each named projection explicitly at authenticatedKernelMember, signedObject, laterEventVariant, and the tag join, or explain why the later record need not retain the digest while still mandating its direct comparison. Add signed-digest mismatch to NT-TCB-KEXEC and the reserved vectors.

verdictBasis: REJECT because ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX; this independent review finds 2 blockers and 2 SHOULD-FIX findings.
conclusion: REJECT. v37 reproduces its custody pins, keeps Linux in D-002 slice 1, preserves authority refusals, confines its semantic diff to the closed roster, rejects raw-wrapper IKCFG pairs, requires a unique selected-payload pair and explicit disabled symbols, and carries a signed text digest. Those changes do not close the proof. The architecture selectors are not joined to the PE code path that executes, and IKCONFIG text remains mutable data with no builder/config-to-code provenance; either defect can qualify a kexec-capable exact kernel. The arm64/decompression grammar is also contradictory and underdetermined, and the token-plus-digest result is not propagated consistently through the closed records and test. DR-126 remains OPEN; no DR is marked SATISFIED, no D-096 (A) grant is minted, and no implementation authority is created.
